title: What Was Left and What Was Forgotten

items.text: The Left and the Forgotten

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Have I looked at myself in my own mirror?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I haven't because the mirror broke. Or did I do so before it shattered?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And Zemfira's prophecy, did it come true?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Disaster will fall on the shards of a broken mirror."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Disaster.
She struggles to search for any useful details in her cluttered mind.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Umm.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No.
Kakania jumps up from her chair, its feet screeching against the marble floor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I remember now.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It did come true. Disaster struck.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It was Elbert's arm.
Clinic

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What brings you here? You haven't recovered yet.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And don't bother. I won't apologize.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But what? Why are you still trying to defend him?! It's because of him that you lost your arm!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What on earth are you thinking?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Those trust fund boys who try to disguise their bullying as "duels." Do you really think that changes the reality of their behavior?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You know I won't sit idly by.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: I know, but I'm still sorry I didn't stop you.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: You can't keep doing this, Klara. It's unseemly to go around roughing people up with your friends from the street, and don't get me started on the horse manure.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I just asked them to join me for a walk, as any lady would do.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If one seldom walks on their own two feet, isn't it normal that one would occasionally trip and fall into some manure? Just blame the fact that horses are allowed in the park.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Or are you suggesting that I bring them to my clinic and expose all their deepest, darkest secrets with my mirrors?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: No, I most certainly am not. Father was already angry about the incident with the hand mirror, and now this.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: You've messed with someone you shouldn't have. His family's reach extends to almost every corner of the affluent classes. It's affected our family business.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father is ... Well, he's furious now, and he may take his anger out on you. So, please, Klara. Come with me to apologize to Ethan before it's too late.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I swear on my life, I have no idea who Ethan even is! I simply beat up a few fair-haired boys I didn't like.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I said I wouldn't apologize, Elbert.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't force me to do anything I don't want to, alright?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: No, Klara, I'm not forcing you. I know that will never work. I'm begging you.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Just this once, alright? Just apologize, and everything will be fine. Father will forgive you, and Mother will be happy, too.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: I'm begging you, Klara.
That same old trick. He knew I couldn't say no to him.
But not this time. I had a way to shut him up.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Then, can I beg for my hand mirror back?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You clearly think if you beg me, I'll do as you wish.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So if I beg you, will you repair and return my hand mirror to me? Exactly as it once was? If you do, I'll apologize.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Well? Can you do as I wish?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You can't, can you?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My mirror will never be the same. Nor will your arm.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And that's why I won't apologize, Elbert.
I thought he'd give up after hearing this.
But, of course, he didn't. Soon after, he paid me another visit. Clearly, the security couldn't turn down a young man with only one arm.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Hey, Klara.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Elbert? Why are you here?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Come in. Let's talk inside.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But if you're here to persuade me to apologize to that man, then don't bother.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: No, actually, I've been thinking about what you said.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: And I'm here to show you something.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Your hand mirror, remember?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: The one given to you by your Roma friend. The one you'd rather break yourself than give over to Father.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: You said that if I fixed it for you, you'd apologize.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's not possible! It was utterly destroyed!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The glass shattered into pieces. How could you possibly put it all back together?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Actually, I did it before you even asked me to. I tried my best to fix it, and I put it in an enamel frame. But I didn't dare give it to you until you said—

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Ahem. Anyway. It's your first hand mirror. Please, take a look.
He reached into the bag on his side and pulled out the mirror.
But before he could hand it to me, I stopped him. What I'd said before was nothing but a shameless taunt.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sorry, but this doesn't fulfill your half of the agreement.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm still not apologizing.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This isn't "exactly as it once was."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at the cracks, and the frame, too. My hand mirror didn't look like this at all.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: A talking wash basin filled with water would do a better job than this. At least that would only show one reflection.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: A talking basin?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ahem, just a metaphor.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In short, it's not so much a mirror as a sign of my failed rebellion. That won't change. No matter how well you fix it, Elbert.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: It's not like that.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara, I repaired it because I wanted to give it back to you, not to make you apologize to Ethan.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: It's not a sign of failure, nor is it useless. This is your very first hand mirror and a gift from a dear friend.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: If it's truly so unimportant to you, then why did you bring it up back then?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Take it back, Klara.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: And please, forgive me for not standing up for you when you confronted Father.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's meaningless, Elbert.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: I know.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: But we don't always live for meaning.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: "Your first hand mirror is for reflecting yourself. Your first table mirror is for observing others."

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: You've helped so many people with the table mirror I gave you, and now,

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: it's time for you to reflect on yourself.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: At least give it a try.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Take a look at yourself in your own mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Elbert ... No, Doctor ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I ... *inhale*

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I still don't understand.
Ask no more, dear Klara.
The illusion's voice is familiar. It's warm and soft.
It is not the voice of any one person, but of many.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you want, Elbert?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: I want you to be free and happy.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: As you want all people to be.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you want, Zemfira?

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: What I want is your safety.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Those who speak out—who pursue their dreams through the tempest—won't flinch at their soaked clothes and the treacherous road ahead.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: I don't want you to get hurt, Klara. I want you to be safe and sound.
You've asked many people the same question, but what's your answer? What do YOU want?
Kakania looks at the shard in her hand.
What do I want?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What, then, is my dream?
The surface of the shard flickers, revealing a mirror reflected in it.
It's the mirror that was once broken, but now it appears whole again.
The hand mirror that she once held so tightly.
